long_biography.plain_text:
After studying economics, Andrey Yakunin entered hospitality through consulting and hotel operations. At Saint Petersburg's Pribaltiyskaya, he helped turn an underperforming Soviet-era complex into a modern hotel and entertainment destination. His share of the eventual investment profit supplied seed capital for his next venture.

Yakunin co-founded VIY Management with Yair Ziv as a private-equity and real-estate investment firm. Its value-add approach centred on acquiring overlooked hospitality assets, renovating them and pairing them with international operators. Projects ranged from the Four Seasons Lion Palace and a Vienna hotel with branded residences to the Antognolla resort estate in Umbria. After selling Antognolla, he continued to describe his work around hospitality, travel and investment initiatives, although his present asset mix is not publicly detailed.
